package.name: dedocs
package.description: Single-file, package-exact, AI-native source for .docx documents.

principles: One text file contains the whole .docx package.
The exact package core stays the source of truth.
Generated guides help orientation but never affect fidelity.
Semantic transforms stay explicit and fail loudly on anchor drift.
Untouched package parts are preserved byte-for-byte.
guarantees: Guides are advisory only and can be regenerated at any time.
Untouched XML is not normalized or reserialized.
Binary parts stay intact as base64 payload blocks.
Zip container timestamps and compression metadata are intentionally out of scope.

commands.name: decompile
commands.summary: Flatten a .docx package into one dedocs file.

commands.name: compile
commands.summary: Rebuild a .docx package from the single-file source.

commands.name: normalize
commands.summary: Refresh hashes, boundaries, and generated guides after hand edits.

commands.name: verify
commands.summary: Compare two .docx packages part-by-part and report exact diffs.

transforms.summary: Apply a literal replacement inside one UTF-8 package part.
Apply inline formatting to a matched span inside one document paragraph.
Attach a Word comment to a matched text span.
Insert a footnote reference and create the footnote entry.
Replace an entire paragraph while preserving paragraph properties by default.
Insert a new paragraph before an anchored paragraph.
Insert a new paragraph after an anchored paragraph.
Delete an anchored paragraph from the document body.
Insert a block table after an anchored paragraph from TSV content.
Insert a block figure after an anchored paragraph using an existing image part.

useCases.title: AI-facing source artifact
useCases.summary: Give an agent one file instead of a zip archive and a directory tree of OOXML parts.

useCases.title: Versionable document workflow
useCases.summary: Review document changes as text with explicit commands instead of archive churn.

useCases.title: Exact package preservation
useCases.summary: Keep untouched package parts byte-exact while still exposing readable guides and transforms.

commandExamples.label: Decompile a real document
commandExamples.result: Flatten the package into one source file with guides and explicit parts.

commandExamples.label: Normalize after hand edits
commandExamples.result: Refresh guide previews, hashes, byte counts, and safe boundaries.

commandExamples.label: Compile back to .docx
commandExamples.result: Rebuild a real Word package from the single-file source.

commandExamples.label: Verify package equality
commandExamples.result: See exactly which package parts differ, or get a clean exact-match result.

quickStart.title: Clone and verify
quickStart.command:
git clone https://github.com/jqdwdty/dedocs.git
cd dedocs
npm test

quickStart.title: Run the document loop
quickStart.command:
dedocs decompile input.docx output.dedocs
dedocs normalize output.dedocs
dedocs compile output.dedocs rebuilt.docx
dedocs verify input.docx rebuilt.docx

playground.note: Browser-side authoring sandbox. It parses real dedocs transform syntax, previews guide-level changes, and reports touched package parts. Full package compile and exact verification still belong to the CLI.

baseParagraphs.text: This is the first paragraph of the introduction. It contains some text about platform governance and political advertising.
The second paragraph discusses Meta's advertising ban and its consequences for electoral transparency.
We developed an automated monitoring system that collected 268,635 advertisements from the Meta Ad Library.
We confirmed 192 accounts as political advertisers that placed a total of 1,329 ads during the campaign period.
The findings document a specific failure mode of platform self-regulation.
